text:
Kasperi Kapanen has gone from 17 points in 41 games last season to a real job in Edmonton: more than 18 minutes a night, a spot on the power play, and ten points in 17 games, seven of them with the man advantage. His top speed ranks at the very top of the league, and his minutes have climbed by about a minute and a half over the last ten games.

How much of it lasts? The power-play production is the part to trust, because it depends on who he's sharing the ice with. At five on five he's around break-even, and Evolving-Hockey's note from last season was blunt: his team created less offense with him on the ice than with almost any forward. He's also scored about a goal more than his chances deserve. His week included a power-play goal and a fight in a loss to Anaheim (RotoWire). Our projection's middle case is about 22 more goals, with a wide range around it, which says the role will decide this season more than the talent.
headline: The fastest man, a bigger role
